newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Eng Kong expects '97 pre-tax profit to grow 13 pct.
newsitem.headline: Eng Kong expects '97 pre-tax profit to grow 13 pct.

text.p: Shipping container logistics group Eng Kong Holdings Ltd forecast its pre-tax profit for financial year 1997 to grow by 13 percent to Singapore $5.2 million, managing director Paul Ng said on Wednesday.
Growth in its core activities -- container handling, repair and transportation -- was expected as Asian ports expand.
"With the expected growth of regional economies and the increasing demand for logistics and logistics infrastructure, there are good prospects for us," Ng said.
"I believe our future growth will come from our new operations in Malaysia, Thailand, Hong Kong and China," said Eddie Li, executive chairman.
Eng Kong plans to heighten presence through acquisition of new ventures or setting up new facilities, Li said.
Turnover was projected to hit S$38.4 million in the financial year ending June 30, 1997 against S$27 million previously, Ng said.
Container traffic in Asia, which accounts for 44 percent of the global traffic in 1995, was expected to rise to 50 percent by 2000, Ng said.

Port demand in Asia was expected to reach 105 million twenty feet equivalent units (TEUs) in 2000 from 61 million TEUs in 1995, he said, noting Singapore and Hong Kong account for over a third of the traffic.
Eng Kong offered 20 million new shares at Singapore $0.56 each on Wednesday. Of the 20 million shares, 15 million would be offered to the public.
All five million placement shares were already fully placed, said Kan Shik Lum, senior vice president of IPO lead manager DBS Bank.
Net proceeds of S$9.8 million raised from the offer would be used to buy equipment and for working capital, Eng Kong said.
